description: Figure 2 illustrates five schematic layer-grouping patterns across four groups, showing how the number of layers is allocated among groups \(G_1\) through \(G_4\) for each pattern. The categories are arranged horizontally as five labeled mini-panels—“Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck”—and within each mini-panel the horizontal direction represents the ordered groups \(G_1, G_2, G_3, G_4\). The vertical dimension represents the number of layers in each group, but no numeric axis line, tick marks, or units are shown; heights are indicated only by the relative bar heights. Each mini-panel contains four light-gray vertical bars with thin dark outlines: in “Increasing,” the bars step upward from left to right (shortest at \(G_1\), tallest at \(G_4\)); in “Uniform,” all four bars are the same height; in “Decreasing,” the bars step downward from left to right (tallest at \(G_1\), shortest at \(G_4\)); in “Spindle,” the two middle bars (\(G_2\) and \(G_3\)) are taller and equal while the two end bars (\(G_1\) and \(G_4\)) are shorter and equal; and in “Bottleneck,” the two end bars (\(G_1\) and \(G_4\)) are taller and equal while the two middle bars (\(G_2\) and \(G_3\)) are shorter and equal. The patterns are presented in a fixed left-to-right order by label, with no additional highlighting, annotations, or legend beyond the pattern names.
